issues.description: Field SealSaloon.stock: the problem statement gives two conflicting requirements. In the descriptive text it asks for "a final Stock stock" initialized in the instance constructor (an instance-level final field) (see problem_statement.md lines 70-72). Later the statement explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static and furthermore lists that 'stock' must be static (see problem_statement.md lines 77-80). The reference solution implements stock as a static final field (SealSaloon.java: line 5 declares 'private static final Stock stock = new Stock();'). This contradiction (instance-level final vs. static final) affects the correct declaration of the field and the required staticness of related methods (acceptSupplyDelivery and calculateTotalPrice) and will confuse students about what to implement and whether those methods should be static.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the requirement in the problem statement consistent. Either: (A) require an instance-level final field (remove the later statement requiring stock to be static) and mark acceptSupplyDelivery/calculateTotalPrice as instance methods, or (B) require a shared stock and state explicitly that stock must be 'static final' and that acceptSupplyDelivery and calculateTotalPrice must be static (as in the provided solution). Update the UML diagram and all textual descriptions so they consistently specify the chosen design (and update examples/tests accordingly). Preferably choose one consistent design (the solution uses static final) and document that choice so students are not left to reconcile contradictory instructions.
